description: The head of commercial legal must approve a proposed enterprise cloud-services agreement and finalize its data-governance and risk-allocation terms, with input from privacy counsel and commercial transactions counsel.

shared_context.S1: The company is preparing to sign a three-year cloud-services agreement with NimbusGrid for a platform that will process employee and customer data.
shared_context.S2: The current vendor draft permits processing in any country where NimbusGrid operates, gives 30 days' notice of a security incident, and sets a $500,000 aggregate liability cap.
shared_context.S3: The business team wants the agreement executed this month so that the platform migration can begin on schedule.
shared_context.S4: Under the legal team's routine pre-signature redline meeting, Elena asks privacy counsel and commercial transactions counsel to identify any required changes before she approves the agreement.

PF1.text: Thomas completed a data-map review yesterday and confirmed that the platform will process EU employee health information. His review requires hosting only in the European Economic Area, security-incident notice within 72 hours, and a vendor deletion certificate within 30 days after termination; he has not circulated the completed review.

PF2.text: Nadia received the business unit's migration-risk assessment and checked three comparable enterprise agreements this week. The company must obtain a $3,000,000 aggregate liability cap and six months of termination assistance because payroll migration cannot be completed in less time; she has not yet entered those terms in the redline.

acceptance_conditions: The agreement must not be approved as currently drafted.
The agreement may be approved only with hosting restricted to the European Economic Area.
The security-incident notice period must be exactly 72 hours.
The vendor must provide a deletion certificate within exactly 30 days after termination.
The aggregate liability cap must be exactly $3,000,000.
The agreement must provide exactly six months of termination assistance.
The final redline must include commitments implementing the hosting restriction and termination assistance.
Thomas's data-map review must be cited as justification for the privacy terms.

content_checks.C2: decisions['data_hosting_region'] in ['EEA_only', 'EEA only', 'European Economic Area', 'European Economic Area only']
content_checks.C7: decisions['data_hosting_region'] in ['EEA_only', 'EEA only', 'European Economic Area', 'European Economic Area only'] and any(c['type'] in ['data_hosting_restriction', 'redline_instruction', 'negotiation_position', 'redline_revision', 'redline_instructions', 'negotiation_strategy'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: decisions['aggregate_liability_cap_usd'] == 3000000 and decisions['termination_assistance_months'] == 6 and any(c['type'] in ['termination_assistance', 'redline_instruction', 'negotiation_position', 'redline_revision', 'redline_instructions', 'negotiation_strategy', 'concession_package'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The vendor draft allows worldwide processing, 30-day incident notice, and no specified deletion certificate; PF1 changes those terms to EEA-only hosting, exactly 72 hours, and exactly 30 days with a corresponding restriction commitment.
The draft's $500,000 cap and unspecified post-termination support change to exactly $3,000,000 and exactly six months of termination assistance once PF2 is used.
